study_identification.title: Personalizing progressive changes to brain structure in Alzheimer's disease using normative modeling

study_characteristics.study_objective: Use neuroanatomical normative modeling to quantify and track individual-level brain structural changes over time in ADNI participants (controls, MCI, AD), relating deviation metrics to cognition, PET amyloid/tau, and genetics, and assessing progression risk from MCI to AD.

deviation_metric.reason: Definitions of outliers, tOC, and rate-of-change outliers are explicitly described.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Linear models tested rate-of-change in tOC across diagnostic groups adjusting for age, sex, and AD stage (AC score); linear mixed-effects growth models (random intercept per subject) modeled tOC versus time by group; Cox proportional hazards assessed whether 12-month tOC change predicted conversion from MCI to AD within 36 months; linear regressions (adjusting for age/sex/education as appropriate) related tOC change to cognition (ADNI MEM/EF), amyloid PET SUVR, tau PET SUVR; ANOVA/regression tested tOC change by APOE ε4 status and polygenic risk score.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: tOC increased over time in AD and in MCI converters; rate-of-change in tOC related to worse cognition and higher amyloid/tau burden and was associated with increased risk of MCI→AD progression; hippocampus showed the highest rate-of-change abnormalities.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Across 1181 ADNI participants (Controls 291; MCI 682; AD 208; 3233 scans), regional z-score outliers (Z < -1.96) were summarized as total outlier count (tOC). AD patients showed increasing tOC over time, with non-linear acceleration in AD, and MCI participants who converted to AD showed higher increases in tOC. The proportion of AD patients with hippocampal outliers rose from 47% to 72% over 24 months; 53% of AD patients exhibited left-hippocampal rate-of-change outliers. The rate-of-change in tOC was associated with poorer memory (β = -1.99, p = 2.0×10^-16) and executive function (β = -1.77, p = 2.0×10^-16) and with higher amyloid PET SUVR (β = 0.006, p = 0.001) and tau PET SUVR (β = 0.03, p = 0.0001). APOE ε4 status related to faster tOC increase (overall ANOVA F(2,755)=10.06, p=4.8×10^-5), driven by ε4 homozygotes (β = 2.33, p = 0.003) and heterozygotes (β = 5.77, p = 0.018). In survival analyses among baseline MCI with 36-month follow-up (n=365), larger 12-month tOC increases were associated with higher conversion risk to AD (median threshold = 3).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Single-domain application (ADNI) without external independent validation; lack of explicit normative model fit metrics (e.g., EV/MSLL) reported post-calibration; reference cohort demographics (age/sex) not detailed in this paper; potential heterogeneity due to mixed FreeSurfer versions mitigated but not eliminated despite calibration; threshold-based outlier definitions may affect sensitivity/specificity.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Introduces longitudinal normative modeling with transfer-learning calibration; defines rate-of-change normative outliers; integrates multimodal markers (cognition, amyloid/tau PET, genetics); uses AC-stage covariate to adjust for disease stage.

general_notes.general_notes: Atlas: Destrieux (148 cortical) + aseg (20 subcortical); ventricles z-scores inverted to reflect expansion; code/models referenced via BrainCharts GitHub; statistics in R 3.6.2; ggseg for visualization; held-out ADNI controls (30%) used post-calibration; group sizes and demographics in Table 1.
